transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-26
Time: 15:00 UTC / 07:00 PT
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samira Voss (Redwood), Tom Reyes (Helmshore), Maya Patel (Helmshore), Luis Ortega (Helmshore), Janelle Kim (Helmshore)

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + rerank flow for Helmshore's product search. Covered Redwood Console demo of reranker endpoint, suggested Optimize recommendations for batching and prefix caching, and discussed enterprise security (SOC2, KMS, SSO). Agreed to pilot: 10k queries/day for 2 weeks, objective 10% relevance lift, cost guardrails. Next steps listed.

Topics:
- Current stack and painpoints
- Live demo: embeddings endpoint, vector store integration, reranking API call pattern
- Console: telemetry, per-route cost/latency, prompt/version pinning
- Optimize suggestions: batching, caching, quant profiles
- Security: VPC/Private, KMS, SSO, retention

Transcript body (timestamps approximate):
00:00 Alex Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood Inference, modern quick hello, joined by Priya and Samira on the SE side. how's everyone doing?
00:07 Tom Reyes: Good, thanks. busy day but excited to see what you have.
00:10 Alex Carter: Awesome. Quick agenda, we'll run through a hosted embeddings + rerank demo, show the console telemetry, then talk security and pilot options. if we have time we'll look at Optimize suggestions. sound ok?
00:20 Maya Patel: Yep sounds good. main reason we're doing this is our current Pinecone + OpenAI flow is getting expensive and latency is spiky on peak.
00:30 Priya Nair: Got it. Priya here — we'll show how Redwood's hosted endpoints combine the embeddings and a lightweight reranker call to improve relevance while keeping p95 latency predictable.
00:45 Luis Ortega: Curious about the rerank model size — do you run a separate model for rerank or is that a tuning on the same embedding model?
00:53 Priya Nair: Great question. we generally use a two-stage pattern: dense retrieval with embeddings, then a compact reranker that runs a cross-attention pass — in hosted mode we serve optimized reranker variants that are lower memory and faster for short contexts. some customers run a larger reranker on dedicated.
01:10 Tom Reyes: So tiers, ok. what's the unit economics vs our current stack?
01:14 Alex Carter: We'll send the live pricing sheet after, but ballpark you should see 20-35% lower unit cost because of combined caching and batching, and we can route most queries to a cheaper rerank variant. Also fewer calls to external LLM provider if you move embeddings to Redwood.
01:30 Janelle Kim: We need SOC2 and KMS for compliance, and SSO through SAML. Also data retention logs — we need audit logs for 1 year.
01:40 Samira Voss: We support SOC2, SAML SSO, and customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private, and we include audit logs in Enterprise packages — we'll share the security pack link.
01:55 Alex Carter: Ok demo time — Priya will drive the console.
02:00 Priya Nair: I'm sharing my screen — first the API pattern: we call /v1/embeddings to vectorize product text, store vectors in your vector DB (or we can host vector storage), then on query we do a top-k retrieval and send N candidates to /v1/rerank which returns scores and a reranked list. here's a sample curl we use, note you can stream tokens for longer contexts but for rerank we do synchronous score returns.
02:25 Priya Nair: (typing) Example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":"Women's navy trench coat, size m"}'
02:45 Maya Patel: Are embeddings dimensionality options fixed? we tuned to 1024 dims in house.
02:51 Priya Nair: We support multiple dims; we can quantize for storage savings and we have recommended dims per model. Optimize will suggest dims/quant profiles given your query distribution.
03:10 Priya Nair: switching to Console — this is the per-route dashboard, you can see token breakdown, call count, p50/p95 latency. here's a rerank route showing average latency 72ms and p95 180ms in our sandbox.
03:30 Luis Ortega: those numbers are promising. are those including network + vector lookup?
03:35 Priya Nair: The dashboard aggregates server-side latency and includes our vector store lookup when hosted. if your vector DB is external it shows network as separate and you can add a tracing hook.
03:50 Tom Reyes: Our biggest issue is tail latency from cold cache — do you do prefix caching or KV cache?
03:56 Priya Nair: yes — we do KV cache for model KV when inline generation is used, and prefix caching for repeated query heads. for rerank we cache embeddings for catalog items and warm popular product vectors, that helps tail a lot. some of the naming in the transcript might show up as KV cash — that's the auto-transcription quirk.
04:20 Maya Patel: On the pilot size, we have a heavy catalog — 1.2M SKUs — vector store size matters. can Redwood host vectors at scale?
04:30 Samira Voss: Absolutely — we have hosted vector layers that handle millions of vectors with sharding and SSD-backed indices. for heavier scale some customers pair Redwood embeddings with managed vector DBs. we'll provide recommended sharding and cost numbers in the pilot plan.
04:48 Priya Nair: Now a quick live rerank example — I'm going to run a sample query "best winter boots waterproof" — it'll hit the retrieval layer, return top 50, then rerank top 10. watch the Console call traces.
05:07 (sound of typing, remote shell)
05:25 Priya Nair: Ok results returned — we're showing the original retrieval order and the reranked order, note the reranker demotes irrelevant seasonal items and bumps product A which has recent user signals. you can also pin a model version so rollouts are deterministic.
05:50 Luis Ortega: How do we evaluate relevance? we currently have golden labels and NDCG metrics.
05:55 Priya Nair: We integrate easily with eval sets — Optimize can run batch evals and give recommendations like tweak embedding model X, reduce candidate pool to 30, or change reranker temperature if you use hybrid scoring.
06:15 Tom Reyes: What about throughput? our QPS spikes to 400 on sale days.
06:22 Alex Carter: For spikes we recommend Redwood Dedicated or reserved capacity; Hosted can handle bursts but Dedicated gives predictable tail latency and committed QPS. We'll show committed qps options in pricing.
06:40 Maya Patel: Do you do auto-fallback if a model is overloaded? e.g., fall back from larger reranker to a cheaper variant?
06:46 Priya Nair: Yes that's a core reliability pattern — smart routing will fallback to compatible model variant by policy, we also support region failover.
07:05 Janelle Kim: Quick security drill — if we want customer-managed keys while using Hosted, is that possible?
07:12 Samira Voss: Short answer: on Hosted we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key via partner KMS integrations for enterprise. For full HSM and airgap you may look at Private.
07:30 Tom Reyes: Ok great. can we see a benchmark comparing your hosted rerank p95 vs our current flow?
07:36 Priya Nair: We'll share a sample benchmark but we'd prefer to run one using your queries to be apples-to-apples. Priya: action item to upload sample benchmark and latency heatmap after you share queries.
07:50 Alex Carter: let's pause for questions before we dive deeper into Optimize.
08:00 Maya Patel: One more — how do we control cost if rerank is expensive?
08:06 Priya Nair: A few levers: lower candidate K from retrieval, use a smaller rerank variant, set dynamic routing by cost thresholds, or use caching aggressively for repeated queries. Optimize can simulate cost impact for each change.
08:30 Tom Reyes: Could we do embeddings on our infra and rerank on Redwood?
08:34 Priya Nair: Yes, hybrid is supported. you can host embeddings locally and call Redwood only for rerank, or vice versa. that sometimes is a good transitional step for customers who want to keep their vector DB.
08:50 (brief silence, people typing)
09:10 Priya Nair: Ok moving to Optimize — this is our cost/perf toolkit. here we upload a sample of real queries and signal distributions, and Optimize suggests batching, quant profiles, and rerank candidate sizes. it also estimates unit cost delta and relevance lift.
09:30 Maya Patel: Can Optimize recommend quantized embedding models? we worry about semantic degradation.
09:35 Priya Nair: Yes it includes A/B style recommendations: try 8-bit quant with dim drop to 768 for low-sensitivity catalogs, or keep 1024 for categories where semantics matter. it reports expected NDCG change based on historical patterns.
09:50 Luis Ortega: If we try those changes and we see regression, do you offer automatic rollback?
09:55 Priya Nair: We have rollouts with canary evaluation and automatic fallback. if quality drops past your threshold we roll back and notify.
10:10 Tom Reyes: Great. I also want to confirm SLAs around uptime and latency — we need an enterprise SLA for Dedicated.
10:17 Alex Carter: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency windows; we'll include the SLA docs in the security pack.
10:30 (fast-forward through demo narration)
20:05 Priya Nair: (demo continues) note the trace includes per-token cost and breakdown so your finance team can map to SKUs. here's an example where rerank adds 12ms and 0.02 cost units per call.
25:00 Maya Patel: small transcription quirk, I see references to "redwood-opt" in the logs — is that internal shorthand?
25:05 Priya Nair: yes, Optimize shows abbreviated labels in the demo, in your account we'll expose more friendly names.
30:10 Janelle Kim: Onboarding timeline? we want to do a pilot in the next 2-4 weeks and then ramp if results are good.
30:18 Alex Carter: That works — our typical pilot is 2 weeks with an agreed eval set, we'll help run a benchmark and then review.
31:00 Tom Reyes: Ok can you also include a diagram for network flow so our infra team can approve?
31:05 Samira Voss: We'll attach a minimal network diagram and VPC peering patterns in the follow-up.
31:22 Alex Carter: Quick note: some words in the transcript may be off — the auto-transcription sometimes turns "KV cache" into "KV cash" or "SAML" into sam-el.
31:40 Maya Patel: lol noted.
32:00 (wrap-up and quick recap)
32:05 Alex Carter: Recap — action items: Alex will send pricing and pilot options, Priya uploads benchmark artifacts, Tom will share sample queries and gold labels. Pilot target: 2 weeks, 10k queries/day, goal 10% NDCG lift + 30% cost reduction.
32:30 Tom Reyes: That sounds right. Also please include security pack and SOC2.
32:35 Samira Voss: Will do.
32:45 Janelle Kim: schedule next meeting for pilot kickoff, preferably next Wed.
32:50 Alex Carter: I'll get calendar invites out after I send the deck and pricing.
33:00 Maya Patel: one more Q — do you have any customers in fashion/retail we can reference?
33:06 Alex Carter: Yes, a few anonymized case studies — we'll include a short customer note with LOE and outcomes.
33:20 Tom Reyes: Thanks everyone, excited to try the pilot.
33:25 Alex Carter: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the links.
33:30 (call ends)
